fusion: The layered twin answers WHERE a scenario should execute and what evidence ceiling that substrate can earn; HostServiceLifecycleWitness answers WHAT typed lifecycle evidence must be observed and bound to target/profile/invocation provenance.

A systemd lifecycle observation inside HRT-TIER-A must be explicitly typed as SIMULATED_TWIN_LIFECYCLE evidence and bound to the Tier-A image/profile identity. It must never reuse or impersonate the exact physical TargetHostProfile identity.

A real HostServiceLifecycleWitness on HRT-TIER-C must bind the exact target_profile_sha256, generation, UID/manager scope and InvocationID and still cannot independently mint external application function readback.
HRT-TIER-B guest lifecycle evidence is likewise simulated evidence even if the guest boots a full systemd instance and reaches active/READY states.

The same witness schema may be reusable across tiers if and only if environment_kind and environment_identity are mandatory provenance fields and CompletionGate applies tier-specific evidence ceilings. Otherwise separate typed producers are safer than an ambiguous universal witness.

recommended_schema_refinement.rule: target_profile_sha256 refers to the physical target only when environment_kind=PHYSICAL_TARGET. Simulators use their own simulation identity and may carry a separate intended_target_profile_ref for comparison, never authority substitution.

counterhypothesis: Separate lifecycle witness schemas per environment kind may be simpler and safer than one generic schema with an environment discriminator.
next_discriminator: At implementation time, test whether one typed witness plus mandatory environment discriminator can make cross-tier provenance confusion structurally impossible. If not, split physical and simulated lifecycle witness types.
